ai.title: SDK 0.3.8 dynamic dirname eval
ai.summary: Bumped @codebuff/sdk to 0.3.8. Updated packages/code-map/src/init-node.ts to fetch __dirname via new Function('return __dirname')() instead of direct reference. Prevents bundlers from inlining absolute paths during build. Internal build fix.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant inside a project folder, it needs to know where files live on your computer so it can find things like ripgrep and the code-map tools. Previously, the build process was accidentally saving your computer's absolute file path right into the tool at packaging time, which broke the assistant whenever the tool was moved to a different folder or machine. Now the tool figures out its own location at runtime instead, so it keeps working no matter where you unzip or install it. This fix is already in place for the published SDK version 0.3.8.

ai.title: Fix ESM/CJS dirname resolution for ripgrep and code-map
ai.summary: SDK 0.3.9 fixes `__dirname` resolution in ESM builds by replacing direct `__dirname` checks with dynamic evaluation via `new Function`. `packages/code-map` extracts this logic into `getDirnameDynamically` in `utils.ts`, updating `init-node.ts` and `languages.ts` to use the helper for tree-sitter WASM path resolution. `sdk/src/native/ripgrep.ts` applies the same dynamic `__dirname` trick for locating bundled `rg` binaries, ensuring correct path construction in both CJS and ESM contexts.

eli5.text: When you run a search or use the AI tools inside the CodeBuff app, the software needs to know where its own helper files live on your computer. In older versions, that lookup broke when the app was packaged in a way called ESM, which meant searches and code analysis could fail silently. Now the app finds its files reliably whether it's running in the older or newer packaging style, so both full-codebase searches and automatic code navigation work again. You won't see anything different in the menus, but things that used to error or hang now just work.

ai.title: SDK v0.3.10 adds dirname try-catch guards
ai.summary: SDK version bumped to 0.3.10. Dynamic `__dirname` resolution in `packages/code-map/src/utils.ts` and `sdk/src/native/ripgrep.ts` wrapped in try-catch blocks to return `undefined` instead of throwing in ESM contexts. This prevents runtime errors during bundled ripgrep path resolution and directory mapping when `__dirname` is inaccessible.

eli5.text: The assistant can stop a specific kind of crash that used to happen when its search tool tried to find files on your computer. When that lookup failed, the assistant would sometimes freeze or show an unhelpful error instead of carrying on. Now it quietly skips that step and keeps working, so searches are less likely to break in the middle of a task. This fix is live today.

ai.title: Fix JSON.stringify typo in SDK README examples
ai.summary: Corrects `JSON.stringifiy` to `JSON.stringify` in `sdk/README.md` event handler examples. Fixes invalid JavaScript syntax in documentation snippets.

eli5.text: The written instructions that show how to set up the assistant contained a small spelling mistake in a command name, so anyone following along would get an error when trying to print out what the assistant is doing at each step. The example now spells that command correctly in both places, so copying the instructions will run without the typo breaking them. If you were already using the tool and not copying those specific example lines, you would notice nothing different today.

ai.title: Add cwd to SDK README example
ai.summary: The SDK README quickstart example now passes `cwd: process.cwd()` to the client configuration. This update aligns the documentation with the SDK's working directory handling requirements. The change is scoped to `sdk/README.md`.

eli5.text: The quick-start guide in the software development kit now shows you adding your current folder location when you start it up, matching how the kit expects to find files it needs to read. If you followed the example before, it might have failed to locate some of the helper tools that search your project; now the instructions match the kit's requirements, so starting it from the guide works as written.

ai.title: Fix wasm and ripgrep bundled paths
ai.summary: SDK v0.3.11 resolves `tree-sitter.wasm` and `ripgrep` binaries across multiple directory structures. `initTreeSitterForNode` now iterates over shared and local WASM paths before falling back to script directory or parent directory checks. `getBundledRgPath` adds a secondary CJS vendor path check for `ripgrep` binaries. This ensures correct binary loading in varied bundling environments.

eli5.text: If you use the AI assistant built on this toolkit, it may have been failing to load its text-parsing and search helper programs when the files were bundled in certain ways. The assistant's file-reading and code-understanding engine should now locate these helper programs reliably across different folder layouts. This resolves intermittent failures when starting up the assistant in custom or unusual installation environments.

ai.title: Docs sidebar switch to CSS sticky
ai.summary: Replaced JS scroll-based `fixed` toggling with CSS `sticky` positioning in `web/src/app/docs/layout.tsx`. Eliminates `isFixed` state and `scroll` listener to prevent layout bouncing. Scope limited to Web docs layout. Height calculation now uses `calc(100vh - 64px - 3rem)`.

eli5.text: When you read a page of the online documentation, the list of chapters on the left side no longer jumps or flickers as you scroll down. Previously, a small program constantly watched your scrolling and then re-locked the list into a fixed position once you scrolled past the top header, which sometimes made the page look jumpy. That watching program has been removed entirely, and the list now simply sticks to the top of your screen using the browser's built-in positioning, so it stays put smoothly as you scroll. This only affects the left-hand chapter list on doc pages and has been live since October 1, 2025.

ai.title: code-map tree-sitter.wasm path resolution
ai.summary: initTreeSitterForNode now resolves web-tree-sitter package root via require.resolve to locate tree-sitter.wasm, replacing sharedWasms loop. Throws explicit error if wasm missing instead of returning preferred path. SDK version bumped to 0.3.12.

eli5.text: When you embed code snippets that need to be parsed by a special tool, the software used to hunt through several backup locations to find a required helper file, and if it couldn't find one, it would return a guess and silently fail. Now it directly asks the helper package where its files were installed and grabs the exact file it needs, throwing a clear error if the file isn't there so you'd immediately notice a broken setup during testing rather than later. Who feels this: only developers working with the code-map package; if you embed and test, you'd now see an explicit warning during startup if the helper file is missing from your bundle, rather than a delayed crash.

ai.title: SDK 0.3.13 simplifies tree-sitter WASM resolution
ai.summary: SDK version bumped to 0.3.13. The `initTreeSitterForNode` function in `packages/code-map/src/init-node.ts` removes a redundant fallback path for `tree-sitter.wasm`. It now strictly checks the shared WASM directory before falling back to the script directory, eliminating an unnecessary local directory check.

eli5.text: The assistant now loads its code-understanding engine from a single, shared location instead of searching a few candidate folders. If you use the SDK, the engine file (a.wasm asset) is found faster because the old extra folder check is gone, so it only tries the shared folder first and the script folder second. The result is the same parsing behavior, just a simpler and slightly more reliable setup behind the scenes.

ai.title: Refine implementation planner prompts and tools
ai.summary: Implementation planner agents now focus on simple, correct solutions over complex ones. The `end_turn` tool was removed from `implementation-planner.ts` as it is no longer needed for the new flow. `plan-selector.ts` updated to prioritize simplicity and reuse, with `includeMessageHistory` set to true. Base prompts in `base-prompts.ts` strengthened the instruction to spawn the max planner for non-trivial tasks.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that drafts code plans now follows a stricter rule: it aims for the simplest, correct solution rather than the most elaborate one. A planning tool that evaluates draft solutions also switched to this 'simple-first' mindset, and it now reads more of the conversation history to make better judgments. Additionally, a guiding prompt for the main assistant was strengthened to explicitly require spawning a detailed planning agent for any non-trivial task, removing any room for skipping it. These changes are live today for internal planning workflows, meaning when you request a multi-step code change, the planning agent you get back will favor minimal, straightforward implementations and won't be allowed to skip that detailed planning step.

ai.title: Tighten tool availability constraints in agent prompt
ai.summary: Updated backend/src/tools/prompts.ts to explicitly restrict agent tool usage. Added instructions forbidding use of unlisted tools, clarifying they may belong to other agents. This prevents hallucinated tool calls by enforcing strict whitelist adherence.

eli5.text: The assistant you interact with now has a stricter rulebook: it can only use the specific tools it's actually given, and it's told not to reach for any others. If you looked, you wouldn't see a visible change in features or behavior, but behind the scenes the prompt instructs the agent not to invent or call tools that don't belong to it, which used to happen when it mistook another agent's tools for its own.

ai.title: Remove dirname checks for tree-sitter.wasm
ai.summary: Removed `hereDir` and `getDirnameDynamically` from `packages/code-map/src/init-node.ts`. `initTreeSitterForNode` now relies solely on `locateFile` fallback to `scriptDir` for `tree-sitter.wasm`. Eliminates runtime directory resolution checks for the shared WASM path.

eli5.text: The software that finds and reads files now stops double-checking where to look for a key helper file each time it starts up. It used to guess the folder location in two different ways and keep the file in several places; now it trusts its built-in search to find the helper wherever it ends up placed. If you watch the startup sequence, you would see one less folder-scan step running, and there would be fewer copies of that helper file stored on disk. The cleanup is in place today for anyone running the internal code-mapping tool.
